title: In view of our cool Universe
caption: A photographer under the Milky Way at ALMA, Chajnantor plateau, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at ALMA, Chajnantor plateau, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: A photographer works beneath the Milky Way, which stretches overhead across the sky above the Chajnantor Plateau. He is Yuri Beletsky, one of ESO's Photo Ambassadors and a member of the ESO Ultra HD Expedition team, busy capturing the cosmos.
This plateau is where ALMA, the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array, is located. It lies high up, some 5000 metres above sea level, and it can become extremely cold there.

The title of the image plays on that cold. ALMA studies what astronomers call the cool Universe: cold gas and dust that give off light at millimetre and submillimetre wavelengths, well beyond what our eyes can see. So while the photographer works on this high, cold plateau to record the sky in visible light, the antennas around him are built to observe some of the coldest material in space.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken in visible light with a camera at ALMA. The camera settings and colour processing are not published.
understand.eye: A long exposure collects more light than the eye can, so the Milky Way looks brighter here than it would to the photographer standing beneath it.

explore: High, dry sites are valuable for this kind of astronomy, because water vapour in the air absorbs much of the millimetre and submillimetre light that ALMA is designed to collect.
alt: A photographer with camera equipment on a high plateau beneath the Milky Way stretching overhead.
